newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU barley sale said worth $142/T, for Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: EU barley sale said worth $142/T, for Saudi Arabia.

text.p: A European Union sale of 183,411 tonnes of German intervention barley is worth $142 per tonne, FOB Germany, and is mostly destined for Saudi Arabia, European grain sources said on Thursday.
The EU's cereals management committee sold the barley at a minimum price of 103.69 Ecus per tonne.
Saudi Arabia provisionally bought 800,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley at an August 21 tender at prices between $160 and $162 including cost, insurance and freight, traders said last week.
But European grain traders and officials said the Saudis may reduce the purchase to 600,000 tonnes.
Traders have said a substantial part of the sale was likely to come from the European Union, which has a supply and freight advantage over other producers.
Substracting freight costs, the equivalent FOB price of the deal is around $142 per tonne.
The EU had signalled it would not part from its barley for less than $149 per tonne, Fob, when news of the deal emerged.
But last week it softened its position, selling 234,324 tonnes of German intervention barley worth some $145 per tonne, FOB Germany.
